memory_candidates.content: When a repo deploys a multi-extension source store into one flat consumer tree (each extension's own scripts/tests/*.sh merged into one shared .claude/scripts/tests/ directory), a lint or data file enumerating 'every discovered test suite' must be checked against the DEPLOYED/merged corpus, not any single extension's own source-store directory -- the merged set is what a test-runner (e.g. run-all.sh) actually discovers and runs in production, and a source-store-only enumeration will systematically undercount by exactly the suites contributed by every OTHER extension. Catch this early by running the new lint's own fixture-test case against the deployed tree, not just the source-store path, before declaring the classification complete.

A corpus-wide lint whose enforcement target is itself part of the test corpus (e.g. 'no unit-class suite may spawn the full test runner') can ride an existing full-battery test-runner gate with ZERO changes to a declarative gate registry: simply add the lint's own fixture suite as a normal discovered test-*.sh file, and the existing full-suite-runner gate executes it on every invocation automatically. This is a stronger form of a 'no new gate row' constraint than extending an existing numbered gate function with a second check -- it requires no gate-registry/dispatcher edit at all, matching a pre-existing lint-without-a-gate-row precedent if one already exists in the corpus (check for it before assuming a new row is needed).
